syntax error.explanation: PHP could not understand the shape of your code and stopped before running any of it. Nothing in the file ran.
syntax error.cause: A missing semicolon, an unclosed brace or quote, or a forgotten $ on a variable. Look at the line ABOVE the one PHP names.

Undefined variable.explanation: You read a variable that has never been given a value. PHP carries on with an empty value, but it is telling you that this was probably not intended.
Undefined variable.cause: A spelling mistake, or a variable set inside an if that did not run.

Undefined array key.explanation: You asked an array for a key it does not have.
Undefined array key.cause: A typo in the key, or reading a key before anything put it there.

Call to undefined function.explanation: PHP could not find a function with that name. Either it is spelled differently, or it is defined in a file that was never included.
Call to undefined function.cause: A spelling mistake, or calling a function before the file that defines it is loaded.

TypeError.explanation: A value of the wrong type was used - passed to a function that declares a different type, or combined with an operator that does not accept it.
TypeError.cause: Text where a number was expected, often straight from user input.

ValueError.explanation: The type was right but the value itself was not allowed for that function.
ValueError.cause: A negative length, an empty array where one item was required, or a value outside the range a function accepts.
ValueError.example:
array_rand([]);        // there is nothing to pick from
array_rand([1, 2, 3]);

DivisionByZeroError.explanation: Something was divided by zero, which has no answer.
DivisionByZeroError.cause: A count or a length that turned out to be 0.

ArgumentCountError.explanation: A function was called with fewer arguments than it requires.
ArgumentCountError.cause: Forgetting an argument, or changing a function's parameters without updating the calls.

ParseError.explanation: PHP could not read the code as PHP at all.
ParseError.cause: Usually a missing <?php at the top of the file, or a stray character in the middle.
ParseError.example:
<?php
echo 'hello';   // every PHP file starts with the opening tag

Error.explanation: A fatal problem stopped the program. The message after the colon says what it was.
Error.cause: Calling a method on something that is not an object, or another mistake PHP cannot recover from.

Exception.explanation: Something threw an exception and nothing caught it, so the program stopped. The message is written by whoever threw it.
Exception.cause: A deliberate throw in your code or a library's, on a condition that turned out to be true.

Undefined property.explanation: You read a property that the object does not have.
Undefined property.cause: A spelling mistake, or a property that is only set in some code paths.

Undefined method.explanation: You called a method that the class does not define.
Undefined method.cause: A spelling mistake, or calling a method on the wrong kind of object.

Cannot modify header information.explanation: Headers must be sent before any output. Something was already printed, so it is too late to set one.
Cannot modify header information.cause: An echo, a blank line, or whitespace before the opening <?php tag.
Cannot modify header information.example:
<?php
header('Content-Type: text/plain');   // must come before any echo
echo 'hello';
